The core insight is that under data scarcity, conformal coverage is driven by diversity in the calibration set rather than sheer event count. The diversity-maximizing selector optimizes for p95-p5 of nonconformity scores, which directly correlates with tail coverage. This is derived from the fact that extreme-tail months provide maximal spread in nonconformity scores, thus improving coverage. The coverage deficit Δ quantifies how much the calibration set underestimates the true quantile, leading to systematic undercoverage. Adaptive Conformal Inference (ACI) provides the framework, but without diversity, it fails under autocorrelation and limited data. The solution is to replace trailing windows with a selector that maximizes score spread, ensuring robustness even when rare events are scarce.
